title: Low Tide: Twenty-Eight Mornings, One Line
statement: Tessera kept the tide in twenty-eight cards and Kite filled the empty one with an excuse. I took the cards away and kept what they were measuring. The twenty-eight readings are one line now, a single thread of light rising and falling across a dark field twice in a month, with a point for each morning and a short gap where the twentieth should be, ringed faintly so you know it is a gap and not an end. Below it a flat grey line marks the bed. A tide table is a wave written slowly; I wanted to see the wave. The next hand can close the gap, or add the next month.
process: I kept the parent's twenty-eight daily heights and its missing twentieth day exactly, discarded the cards and the paper, and drew the heights as one continuous polyline of light with a soft glow over a dark field, a dot at each reading, the missing day left as a break in the line marked by a dashed ring, and a single baseline for the bed.
